claim: A packaged build now contains seanime.exe at exactly the path exePath.ts resolves for a packaged app: <resourcesPath>/seanime/seanime.exe.
authorization: The user was asked and chose 'Edit forge.config.ts now', explicitly overriding CLAUDE.md's rule against altering root project configuration. The licensing consequence was stated in the question and is recorded below.

howItWorks.staging: prePackage copies the resolved binary to build/seanime/seanime.exe. electron-packager copies each extraResource entry into the resources root by basename, so build/seanime becomes <resources>/seanime.
howItWorks.source: SEANIME_EXE if set, else the pinned ../seanime-upstream/seanime.exe — the same dev rule exePath.ts uses.
howItWorks.failsLoud: A missing binary throws and fails the build. The failure this prevents is a package that installs cleanly and has a dead media surface on every screen.
howItWorks.escapeHatch: SEANIME_SKIP_SIDECAR_PACKAGING=1 packages without one, with a warning, and removes any stale staged exe.
howItWorks.nonWindows: prePackage receives the platform; a non-win32 target gets an empty slot rather than a .exe (the makers include deb/rpm).
howItWorks.emptyDirIsDeliberate: The staging directory is always created. extraResource throws ENOENT on a missing path, and an empty slot still yields exePath.ts's actionable 'seanime.exe not found. Tried: …' message.

notProven.what: The packaged app was not launched to watch its sidecar come up ready.
notProven.why: The debug bridge only exists in dev-server mode, so a packaged run could only be driven by Windows mouse/keyboard control, which is a standing user instruction never to do with this app. What is proven is that the binary sits at the exact resolved path, byte-identical; what is inferred is that app.isPackaged/resourcesPath then behave as the unit tests specify.
notProven.howToClose: Launch the packaged app manually with SEANIME_SIDECAR=1 and open the Media workspace once.
